messages:
Alex: Heads-up: we should add a tiny "migration checklist" section for customers moving from Hosted -> Dedicated that specifically calls out autoscale cooldowns, isolation decorators, and how fallback interacts with committed capacity. Tickets keep coming in asking why autoscale behaves differently. cc @tara @kevin

Tara: Yep — short, actionable bullets would help. Can we include a CLI snippet and a note about recommended cooldown defaults (e.g., 60-90s) and why?

Kevin: I can draft a CLI + YAML pair. Quick note: cooldown ties into batching/kv-cache warmups; shorter cooldowns can increase thrash and latency. Recommend 60s for small fleets, 90s+ for larger reserved pools.

docs-bot: Created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321 (WIP) — adding migration checklist and snippets.

Alex: Draft checklist (keep very short):
- Verify reserved_capacity and target_qps map to your traffic sims.
- Set scalePolicy.cooldown_s to 60-120s depending on workload.
- Add tenant_labels.isolation to reflect preemption tolerance (low/medium/high).
- If using fallbackModel, ensure fallback_policy.max_fallback_pct is explicit.
- Test with a small canary before full migration.

Kevin: CLI snippet for ops folks who prefer terminal examples:
```bash
# set a scale policy with cooldown and fallback via redwoodctl
redwoodctl provision update --tenant acme-corp \\n  --reserved-gpus 4 \\n  --model rdl-large-v1 \\n  --scale-target-qps 150 \\n  --scale-cooldown 90 \\n  --fallback-model rdl-medium-q1 \\n  --fallback-max-pct 30 \\n  --label isolation=medium
```

Tara: +1. Can we add a one-liner about SDK behavior too? Some customers use SDK-level routing_preferences that can opt out of fallback per-request.

Kevin: SDK note (JS):
```js
// per-request override to disable fallback
client.generate({
  model: 'rdl-large-v1',
  prompt: 'Explain retention policy',
  routing_preferences: { allow_fallback: false }
});
```

sre-jen: Ops caveats: 1) Preemption vs fallback: preemption may evict unreserved workloads before fallback triggers for reserved tenants. 2) SLA language: migration docs should stress that fallback does NOT reduce contracted reserved throughput guarantees, but it may affect latency SLOs for a subset of requests if fallback used.

Alex: Good catches. I'll add an explicit bullet: "Fallback = best-effort overflow; reserved throughput remains contractually guaranteed." Also add a link to the SLA doc and to the shard-failover runbook (internal links).

Tara: Minor editorial request: change "cooldown_s" -> "cooldown_s (seconds)" in the YAML example so non-dev readers don't get confused. Also include a tiny troubleshooting FAQ item: "Why did my tenant see 25% fallback?" -> explain max_fallback_pct + quota exhaustion vs reserved limits.

docs-bot: PR updated with CLI, YAML, SDK snippets, checklist, and FAQ. Reviewers requested: @alex @kevin @sre-jen

Kevin: I'll review wording on the SLA bullet and the ops caveats later today. If clean, I can approve and merge.

Alex: Thanks — I'll follow up with a traffic-sim example in a separate PR. Planning to add a small script that toggles fallback pct for canaries.

Tara: Thanks all, this will reduce a lot of tickets.

Alex: Merged after minor copy edits. Closing thread. :tada:
